problem_statement: The Urara documentation starter is a multi-page SvelteKit content site — a home overview that lists the docs entries as post cards with a row of topic tags, a Hello World getting-started page, and its Elements and ToC-disabled sub-pages, all under a shared header and footer. The home already lets a reader tap a topic tag to narrow the post list, but the control is bare: there is no heading, no result count, and nothing tells the reader how many of the docs match the active topic. Turn the home tag row into a proper 'Docs finder': a labelled filter panel above the post feed with the topic tabs and a live count readout that reads 'Showing N of M · <label>' and updates on every tab click (for example, tapping #Elements narrows the feed and the readout to 'Showing 2 of 6 · #Elements'). Then add a small cross-page 'Docs finder index' — a topic link strip that repeats on the home overview and on every docs post page (Hello World, Elements, ToC-disabled) so a reader can jump back to a filtered view from anywhere. Requirements: (1) the finder index must appear on the home overview AND all docs post pages, (2) the filter tab row must wrap responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) the finder and post grid must keep the site's quiet slate/gray minimalist styling — legible cards, not a collapsed dark-on-dark pile, and (4) the count readout must stay in sync with the active topic so it never shows a stale total. Keep the header navigation, existing page content and the static SvelteKit build intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Turn the home tag row into a labelled 'Docs finder' panel above the post feed: a 'Docs finder' heading, the topic tab row, and a live 'Showing N of M · <label>' count readout.
Add a shared 'Docs finder index' topic-link strip that renders on the home overview AND every docs post page (Hello World, Elements, ToC-disabled) — a shared component, not a per-page copy.
The filter tab row must wrap responsively so no page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the finder panel and the post cards in the site's quiet slate/gray minimalist language (legible bordered chips and light cards), not a collapsed off-palette dark-on-dark block.
Wire the count readout to the active filter: after clicking a topic tab, the readout must update to 'Showing 2 of 6 · #Elements' (the live matched count), never a stale 'Showing 6 of 6'.
author_notes: Built on the importantimport Urara SvelteKit documentation starter (a shared header and footer under the site layout, a minimalist daisyUI slate/gray palette, MDsveX-rendered content pages and the home feed's own topic tag filter). The Docs finder upgrades that native tag filter with a live count readout and a shared cross-page docs finder index component; three real docs posts (configuration, deploying, markdown-syntax) were added so the count spans six entries. No remote assets are added — the demo domain and PWA service worker were neutralised and the placeholder author bio replaced so the static SvelteKit build is fully offline with zero console or network errors; the site's own sakura avatar image and manifest icons are the only imagery.
design_constraints: Implement the Docs finder index as a shared component invoked from both the home overview and the post container so a single source of truth reaches every page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The filter tab row must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile; the tab spacing must stay legible.

The finder panel and post cards must adopt the site's slate/gray palette and minimalist typography so the feed reads as part of the docs site; the post cards must stay legible and must not overlap or shingle into an unreadable pile.
The count readout must re-derive its 'Showing N of M' value from the currently matched posts after every tab click, so it can never go stale relative to the visible filtered feed.
Do not remove or regress the header navigation, footer, existing page content or the static SvelteKit build; keep the site free of console and network errors.

change_completion: The Docs finder index is present on the home overview and on the Hello World and Elements docs post pages (the shared component reaches every route).
After clicking the #Elements topic tab on the home page, the count readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 · #Elements' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 6 of 6'.
design_consistency: The Docs finder and post feed match the reference's slate/gray minimalist styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not a collapsed dark-on-dark pile.
The finder adopts the site's slate chip idiom and legible light cards so it reads as part of the docs site across every page.
responsive: No captured page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the filter tab row wraps.
desktop_finder_home, mobile_finder_home and mobile_initial keep the Docs finder readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Header navigation, the footer and the page headers remain present and functional.
The existing home/Hello World/Elements/ToC content and the static SvelteKit build are not removed or broken; the site stays free of console and network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the home overview, the Docs finder panel and the responsive shell.
desktop_post, mobile_post, desktop_elements, mobile_elements and desktop_toc protect the existing docs pages and carry the Docs finder index.
desktop_finder_home and mobile_finder_home scroll the Docs finder into view and must show the slate/gray finder without horizontal overflow.
desktop_index_post and desktop_index_elements protect the Docs finder index's presence on the Hello World and Elements post pages (the cross-page rollout).
toggle_filter_home clicks the #Elements topic tab; the count readout must then read 'Showing 2 of 6 · #Elements'.
